messages.subject: Matrix is not positive definite
parts:
Hello,

I am fitting a negative binomial model to estimate infant mortality with a random intercept and random slope on year by region, along with a Beag spatial intercept on region with a number of fixed effects. The model is of the form

model <- deaths ~ f(id1, model="iid") +  f(id2, year, model="iid") + f(id3, model="besag", graph.file=graphFile, param=c(1,0.01)) + year +  m.age + income.percapita

and is fit with the statement

inla(model, family="nbinomial", E=births, data=data, control.compute=list(dic=1,cpo=1))

The id variables represent 490 regions. I am getting the following error

        GMRFLib version 3.0-0-snapshot, has recived error no [2]

        Reason    : Matrix is not positive definite

        Function  : GMRFLib_factorise_sparse_matrix_TAUCS

        File      : smtp-taucs.c

        Line      : 698

        RCSId     : file: smtp-taucs.c  hgid: 0b6187069b39  date: Mon Jul 05 11:53:43 2010 +0200

I am having trouble pinpointing the source. It appears that this seems to happen randomly, as I can get the model to fit if I submit it repeatedly. This make me think I might be able to get a consistent fit with the right initial values. Can you give me any advice?

Thanks
Casey

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Matrix is not positive definite
parts:
can you retry after doing a

inla.upgrade(testing=TRUE)

??

you seem to use a (very) old version.

H
